body:
[A10] AMENDMENT: PocketBeagle 2 variant (the board the bench now uses, per the owner's note above). The roles, the frame format, the electrical rules and the "what this does not claim" section of the recipe are unchanged; only the SoC-side header, the McASP instance and the serializer numbering differ. Target: PocketBeagle 2 rev A1 (AM6254), McASP0, synchronous four-wire tree. It is NOT the original PocketBeagle (AM3358).

## Wiring: AX7101 J11 to PocketBeagle 2 P1/P2 (McASP0, pad mux mode 0)

| Signal | AX7101 J11 pin (FPGA ball) | Direction | PocketBeagle 2 pin (McASP0 signal) |
|---|---|---|---|
| BCLK, 12.288 MHz | 6 (B20) | FPGA to SoC | P2.01 (ACLKX) |
| FSYNC, 48 kHz | 8 (F19) | FPGA to SoC | P1.04 (AFSX) |
| DOUT, the FPGA's rendered 8 channels | 5 (A20) | FPGA to SoC | P2.03 (AXR1, receive serializer) |
| DIN, the FPGA's captured 8 channels | 7 (F20) | SoC to FPGA | P1.02 (AXR0, transmit serializer) |
| GND | 1 | shared | P1.15 |
| GND | 37 | shared | P1.16 |
| GND | 38 | shared | P2.15 |

Seven conductors: four signals, three grounds (spare grounds P1.22 and P2.21). Serializer 0 transmits and serializer 1 receives; crossing the two data wires gives a link where both ends drive the same wire.

## Pins to leave open on the PocketBeagle 2

- P1.14 and P2.23 (3.3 V expansion rails) and every VIN, 5 V or USB rail: no power rail between the boards. The SoC board powers from its own USB-C; do not drive any of its I/O while it is unpowered.
- P1.08 (ACLKR, shared with the UART1 transmit pad): the boot firmware muxes it as an OUTPUT. An FPGA output landed here drives into a driven pin. P1.06, P1.10 and P1.12 stay open as well. P1.02 and P1.04 sit two positions from P1.06 and P1.08: count the pins twice on the P1 end.
- Each of the four McASP0 header pins is a two-ball pin. The TDM8 device tree parks each partner ball as a GPIO input; boot that tree BEFORE the FPGA drives the header, otherwise a partner ball can come up at its reset function and drive against the FPGA.

## Wire by header pin number, never by ball name

The two packages share ball names with different meanings. `A20` is the trap: it is the FPGA's render output (J11.5) and, on the SoC, the ACLKR pad behind P1.08 that must stay open.

## Electrical and continuity

The AX7101 header's on-board 33 ohm series resistors are the source termination; fit nothing extra unless a scope shows ringing at P2.01. Unpowered, each signal wire reads about 33 ohm from the J11 pin's FPGA side to the SoC header pin; a dead short means a power or ground pin, that is the wrong pin. Every signal wire is open to every other and to ground; J11.2, J11.39, J11.40, P1.14, P2.23, P1.06 and P1.08 have nothing landed on them.

## Image and software notes

- Use a bitstream built from `dev` at or after 9c423e2c (PR #454, #452): earlier images launch FSYNC on the rising BCLK edge, zero setup to a rise-sampling McASP.
- The stock k3-udma driver retires the cyclic receive descriptor after one period on this SoC's BCDMA, so a capture dies after the first period with an I/O error. The bench kernel carries a three-hunk fix; with it an 8-channel, 32-bit, 48 kHz capture runs to its full length. This is a SoC-side software fact and changes nothing on the wire.
- First light: SoC board first, then the AX7101; scope P2.01 (12.288 MHz) and P1.04 (48 kHz, one BCLK wide) at the header pin; then capture, then per-channel tones on render. All zero on render points at FSYNC polarity or the wrong serializer; a one-slot rotation points at the data delay.

The "Before trusting audio" checklist of the recipe applies unchanged, with the scope points above and the image floor raised to 9c423e2c. Results go under #448.
